question.leadin: The Battle of Inchon was a major offensive in this conflict, and this war ended with the establishment of the Demilitarized Zone at the 38th Parallel.
question.text: Name this conflict that ended with an armistice dividing a namesake peninsula.
question.answerHtml: Korean War [accept “Conflict” in place of “War;” or Hanguk Jeonjaeng; or Choguk haebang chonjaeng]
question.clue: A commander on one side of this war proposed dropping 30 to 50 nuclear bombs on an opponent in order to create a radioactive wasteland and was criticized for rudeness to his country's leader at Wake Island.

swap.leadin: Operation Paul Bunyan involved the use of overwhelming military force to chop down a tree in this area.
swap.text: Name this area which separates North and South Korea from each other. The Joint Security Area within this zone is used for diplomatic meetings.

question.leadin: Answer the following about a certain class of warship.
question.text: An earlier example of an ironclad warship was this type of ship developed by Admiral Yi Sun-sin to resist a 16th century Japanese invasion of Korea. Named for the shape of the animal on its bow, these ships boasted cannons and a hull covered in spikes.
question.clue: Soldiers from Ming China helped defend Korea from Japanese invasion at the end of the 16th century. During that conflict, Korean Admiral Yi utilized these crazy awesome vessels which received their name from the appearance caused by their armored decks.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about yellow ribbons in history.
swap.text: Victims of the Sewol ferry disaster in this country are commemorated with yellow ribbons. The Miracle on the Han River refers to massive growth in this country's capital of Seoul.
swap.answerHtml: South Korea [or the Republic of Korea; or ROK; prompt on Korea; reject “North Korea” or the “Democratic People’s Republic of Korea”]
swap.clue: Nearly 300 high school students drowned on a ferry boat in this country in 2014.

question.text: During the lead up to this time period, the forces of Sun Quan and Liu Bei used fire ships to turn back the much larger force of Cao Cao at the Battle of Red Cliffs. This time period followed the collapse of the Han dynasty.
question.clue: The "Later" part of a period with this name was dominated by a Unified Silla that conquered Goguryeo.

swap.leadin: It was part of Operation Chromite.
swap.text: Name this amphibious invasion and decisive U.N. victory during the Korean War in September 1950 that would allow for the subsequent retaking of the Kimpo airfield and the recapture of Seoul.
swap.clue: The USS Mansfield, USS Swenson, and USS Collett bombarded a fortress in the early stages of this battle, which saw the X Corps land at Green, Blue, and Red beaches.

question.leadin: This leader was referred to as "supreme leader", as well as "Dear Leader" and "Generalissimo"
question.text: Identify this leader of North Korea from 1994 to 2011. He died on December 17, 2011 of a heart attack.
question.clue: His "Sunshine policy" tried to bolster the software industry, and he once abducted a movie director to shoot a socialist Godzilla flick.

swap.leadin: A member of this family has the title "Eternal President" and ordered the Blue House Raid into a neighboring country.
swap.text: Name this family that created the Juche [JOO-chey] ideology for their Workers Party. A member of this family was killed with V་X nerve agent at Kuala Lumpur Airport.
swap.clue: The ideology of Juche was developed by members of this family given the posthumous titles "Eternal Chairman" and "Eternal President."

question.leadin: June 25 will mark the 50th anniversary of the start of the Korean War. Answer these questions on the conflict.
question.text: When the U.N. approved the reunification of Korea as a military goal, the Chinese army entered to support the North Koreans, crossing this river.
question.clue: The Friendship Bridge is the only remaining bridge over this river and connects the cities of Dandong and Sinujiu.

swap.leadin: Name these sites important to the Korean War.
swap.text: On September 15, 1950, U.S. Marine Commander Lewis B. Puller led United Nations forces in a landing on this island west of Seoul.
swap.clue: In September, 1950, American forces launched an amphibious assault at this location 100 miles north of the Pusan Perimeter, driving the North Koreans back and leading to the recapture of Seoul.

question.leadin: This kinship system was weakened by the 1746 Dress act, which prohibited wearing kilts or identifying patterns.
question.text: What name is given to these family and extended groups identified by their differing tartans?
question.clue: What are these kinship groups in which members often took the chief's surname and which often have a distinctive tartan pattern?

swap.text: Both the Korean War and the Pueblo incident were ended by negotiations in this central Korean village on the Kyongui road.
swap.clue: This village which hosted a more famous conference that led to the armistice between United Nations forces and communists in 1953 during the Korean War.

question.text: Members of this Joseon noble, scholarly class were expected to be knowledgeable in the Confucian classics. To enter this class, one had to perform well on the gwageo civil service exam.
question.clue: This class which constituted the aristocracy of a kingdom which was the last to select its officialdom through the gwageo examination system.

swap.leadin: These campaigns are sometimes called the "Ceramic Wars" because potters were kidnapped and moved to Arita, where they developed one country's porcelain industry.
swap.text: Name these campaigns during which soldiers reportedly cut off the noses of their victims as trophies because heads were too unwieldy to haul around.
swap.answerHtml: Japanese invasions of Korea [accept Hideyoshi’s invasions of Korea; accept Imjin Wars]
swap.clue: An opponent of one of these was Admiral Yi Sun-shin, who utilized turtle ships.

question.text: While the Sui had directly intervened in Korea, The Tang instead took the approach of allying with this southeasternmost of Korea's Three Kingdoms. This kingdom utilized the "bone-rank" caste system.
question.clue: This dynasty employed a cultured class of cosmetic-using soldiers called the "flowering knights," or "hwarang."

swap.leadin: This kingdom is traditionally said to have been founded by Hyokkose.
swap.text: Name this kingdom that unified a peninsula after conquering neighboring Paekche and Koguryo with the help of the Tang Dynasty, then expelled Tang forces.
swap.clue: This kingdom included the hereditary "head rank 6" caste in its "bone rank" system, and used highly-educated elite knights whose name means "flower boys."

question.leadin: Guerrillas in this uprising set up bases in the caves around Hallasan, an extinct volcano where remains of victims can still be found, and attacked paramilitary troops of the Northwest Youth League.
question.text: Name this massacre that lasted over a year from April 1948 to 1949, in a nation being occupied under Operation Blacklist Forty.

swap.leadin: An inscription written on the Seven-Branched Sword describes how it was made by a crown prince of this kingdom.
swap.text: Name this kingdom whose last ruler, Uija ("ooh-EEH-jah"), was the progenitor of the Kudara no Konikishi clan. Yamato-era Japan lost 800 ships attempting to save this kingdom, whose incorporation into a larger kingdom was followed shortly by a similar conquest of Goguryeo ("GO-goo-r'yuh").
swap.clue: This kingdom absorbed all of the lands of the Mahan confederacy, thus seizing all of the present-day Jeolla ("jul-lah") region, under its great ruler Geunchogo ("geun-choh-goh").

question.leadin: Now located at the National Library of France, it was composed by the Buddhist monk Baegun around 1372 AD, and published by his students Seoksan and Daldam. FTPE.
question.text: Name this two-volume Korean anthology of Zen Buddhist teachings which is the oldest existing metal-plate printed book.

swap.leadin: This man's date with the bottom of the ocean in 1973 may have been averted through the quick action of ambassador Philip Habib, whom he later credited with helping to inspire his Nobel-winning Sunshine Policy.
swap.text: Identify this politician who failed thrice in his bid for the Presidency when not enduring hunger strikes, house arrests, or exile, prior to becoming the first Jeolla native to achieve the office.
swap.clue: Ambassador Philip Habib and Henry Kissinger supposedly intervened during an incident in which this man had weights tied to him and was almost drowned after he was kidnapped from a hotel in Tokyo.
